Vs.
Golam Mostafa and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 5. Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Additional District Judge committed an error of land in not applying the settled principle of law that none but the contracting par-ties and the Government should be parties in the instant suit for specific performance of contract that the Additional District Judge committed an error of law in allowing the civil revision and application of the applicant No. 1-11 for addition as defendant in the suit on the ground of avoiding multiplicity of suits or proceedings in the face of his own finding that already there were suits between the applicants and defendants and the applicants lost the suits and appeals arising therefrom and the applicants preferred civil revision against the appellate decree and in not considering that the applicants are not entitled in law to agitate the question of title against the defendants at the trial stage of the instant suit. The learned Advocate further submitted that the rejection of the application of the applicant No. 1-11 for addition ad defendants in the suit occasioned miscarriage of justice without considering that the fate of the existing parties to the suit in respect of suit property would be subject to the result of the Civil Revision No. 1362 of 2003 and hence the applicants would not be prejudiced in any manner for not being par-ties   in the present suit; that the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is not proper judgment of affirmance inasmuch as the High Court Division has not controverted the judgment of the Court of Appeal  and trial court below on consideration of evidence on record. The learned Advocate finally submitted that in a suit for specific performance of contract a third party is not a necessary party whose presence before the Court is not necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all the question in the suit and the petitioner is claiming spec if is performance for 0.18 acres of land whereas the applicants arc claiming 22½ acres of land. The petitioners submit that since the petitioners are not claiming any relief against the applicants, they have been illegally added as defendants in the suit.
